brand.name: Byte Sized
brand.tagline: Tech history, one minute at a time

scenes.text: How computers went from filling a room to fitting in your pocket.
In 1946, ENIAC was unveiled: thousands of vacuum tubes filling a whole room.
In 1947, Bell Labs built the first transistor, a tiny switch with no glowing tubes.
In 1958, Jack Kilby put a whole circuit on one piece of material: the integrated circuit.
In 1969, ARPANET carried its first message between two universities in California.
In 1991, the World Wide Web opened to the public.
And in 2007, the iPhone put the internet in your pocket.
